beats.text: Type sine of one hundred and twenty degrees into any calculator, and it answers instantly: zero point eight six six.
beats.spoken: Type sine of one hundred and twenty degrees into any calculator, and it answers instantly: zero point eight six six.

beats.text: But no right triangle has a one-hundred-and-twenty-degree angle. Not a single one.
beats.spoken: But no right triangle has a one-hundred-and-twenty-degree angle. Not a single one.

beats.text: Sine of minus thirty degrees? Minus one half. Sine of a thousand degrees? It answers that too.
beats.spoken: Sine of minus thirty degrees? Minus one half. Sine of a thousand degrees? It answers that too.

beats.text: Those numbers don't come from soh cah toa. They come from a single point, running around a circle.
beats.spoken: Those numbers don't come from soh cah toa. They come from a single point, running around a circle.

beats.text: And that circle, seen from the side, is hiding inside every wave: sound, light, even the power in your wall.
beats.spoken: And that circle, seen from the side, is hiding inside every wave: sound, light, even the power in your wall.

beats.text: Trigonometry is more than two thousand years old, and for most of that time it was a tool for the sky, not for homework.
beats.spoken: Trigonometry is more than two thousand years old, and for most of that time it was a tool for the sky, not for homework.

beats.text: In this video, I want to follow it from the stars, to the circle, to the waves, and answer three questions with you.
beats.spoken: In this video, I want to follow it from the stars, to the circle, to the waves, and answer three questions with you.

beats.text: One. Why does every angle come with its own fixed number, its sine?
beats.spoken: One. Why does every angle come with its own fixed number, its sine?

beats.text: Two. How can a calculator find the sine of an angle that no triangle can hold?
beats.spoken: Two. How can a calculator find the sine of an angle that no triangle can hold?

beats.text: And three. Why does that same circle turn up inside every wave?
beats.spoken: And three. Why does that same circle turn up inside every wave?

beats.text: It all begins with a problem much older than any calculator: measuring something you can't reach.
